node.label: John Tosh
node.date_label: “What Should Historians Do with Masculinity?” (1994) · A Man’s Place (1999) · Manliness and Masculinities in Nineteenth-Century Britain (2005)
node.description: A historian of masculinity and historical practice. In his 1994 essay he distinguishes public ideals of manliness from the social production of masculine status, linking household, workplace and male associations. His public-history essay argues that historical context, contested interpretation and careful analogy belong to democratic judgment. These are two particular methodological proposals; the entry does not reduce masculinity to an unchanging male essence or treat a later paperback as the original book.
node.representative_figures_and_works: “What Should Historians Do with Masculinity?” (1994); A Man’s Place (1999; paperback 2007); Manliness and Masculinities in Nineteenth-Century Britain (2005).
node.scope_note: New identity matched to Roehampton historian and masculinity titles. Primary OCR excerpt and author policy essay support bounded arguments. No claim that OCR is an authenticated exact transcription, that all work is read, or that one masculinity describes all classes and periods. Original, paperback and collected-essay dates distinct.
